title: Signed dual models and Tor windows for split-perfect sheaf complexes
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use sheaves of $B$-modules and their unbounded derived category $D(B)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $a\le b$ be integers and $E^\bullet$ a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $E^r=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. Suppose each degree has specified maps $E^r\xrightarrow{i_r}B^{\oplus N_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}E^r$ with $N_r\in\mathbf N$ and $p_ri_r=1$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]; these maps are not assumed to be chain maps. Define $D^\bullet=\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0])$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-hom-complex], and let $E^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_B(E^\bullet,B[0])$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Use ordinary sheaf tensor and its K-flat derived tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-kflat-complex].

Every functor $E^r\otimes_B-$ and $\mathcal Hom_B(E^r,-)$ is exact. For every K-injective resolution $B[0]\to I^\bullet$, the induced map $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0])\to\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism; consequently $D^\bullet$ represents $E^\vee$. Explicitly,
$$D^n=\mathcal Hom_B(E^{-n},B),\qquad d_D^n(\phi)=(-1)^{n+1}\phi\circ d_E^{-n-1},\qquad D^n=0\ (n\notin[-b,-a]).$$
The maps $p_{-n}^*$ and $i_{-n}^*$, with star denoting precomposition, give a splitting
$$D^n\xrightarrow{p_{-n}^*}\mathcal Hom_B(B^{\oplus N_{-n}},B)\xrightarrow{i_{-n}^*}D^n,\qquad i_{-n}^*p_{-n}^*=1,$$
and the middle term is isomorphic to $B^{\oplus N_{-n}}$. Both $E^r$ and $D^n$ are flat, meaning their sheaf tensor functors are exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every sheaf $M$ of $B$-modules placed in degree zero, cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] satisfy
$$H^q(E^\bullet\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}M)=0\quad(q\notin[a,b]),\qquad H^q(E^\vee\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}M)=0\quad(q\notin[-b,-a]).$$
No constant-coefficient, enough-points or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08JH (lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect), K-injective comparison; Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), strict-perfect dual terms; Tag 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude), implication (2) to (1). Extracts the exact-term, signed dual and flat-Tor calculations of returned parent proof steps 3-5.

proof.text: For each integer $r$, apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-finite-retract-dual-exact] with $R=B$, $T=E^r$, $i=i_r$ and $p=p_r$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given finite rank and $p_ri_r=1$. Its exact-Hom clause proves that $\mathcal Hom_B(E^r,-)$ sends short exact sequences to short exact sequences. This is internal Hom exactness; no assertion about projectivity for global sections is needed.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, finite-free/direct-summand calculation; exact-Hom retract as in Tag 08JH

proof.text: Here is the elementary tensor counterpart. For any finite-free retract $T\xrightarrow{i}B^{\oplus N}\xrightarrow{p}T$, the maps $i\otimes1$ and $p\otimes1$ give a natural retract of $T\otimes_B-$ from $B^{\oplus N}\otimes_B-\cong(-)^{\oplus N}$. The last isomorphism is induced by $(b_j)\otimes m\mapsto(b_jm)_j$, with inverse $(m_j)\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes m_j$, first on presheaves and then on their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A finite direct sum of a short exact sequence is short exact: kernels are coordinatewise and local lifts for finitely many coordinates exist on a common refinement. Exactness passes to the displayed natural retract: include a kernel element in the finite-power sequence, lift it from the previous term locally, and project that lift by $p\otimes1$; naturality and $(p\otimes1)(i\otimes1)=1$ give the required preimage. The same inclusion/projection proves injectivity on the left and local surjectivity on the right. Thus $T\otimes_B-$ is exact. Taking $T=E^r$ proves its tensor exactness and hence flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; commutativity of $B$ interchanges the tensor factors.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, finite-free retract calculation; elementary exactness argument using sites-modules.tex definition-flat

proof.text: Let $f:B[0]\to I^\bullet$ be any of the K-injective resolutions in the statement. It is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] with $P=E^\bullet$, $M=B[0]$ and $N=I^\bullet$: the finite interval is $[a,b]$, and the exact-term hypothesis is step 1. It gives exactly the asserted quasi-isomorphism $D^\bullet\to\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$, even if $I^\bullet$ is unbounded in both directions. In particular take the fixed K-injective resolution used in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For that choice the target represents $E^\vee$ by definition, so $D^\bullet$ represents it as well. The comparison assertion already proved holds for every choice of $f$.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect, K-injective comparison; section-internal-hom, K-injective construction

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-bounded-dual-components] with $R=B$ and the given bounds. Projection to the unique possibly nonzero factor gives $D^n=\mathcal Hom_B(E^{-n},B)$ under the canonical identification and $D^n=0$ outside $[-b,-a]$. Its differential formula is $d_D^n(\phi)=(-1)^{n+1}\phi d_E^{-n-1}$, exactly the sign in the statement. In particular there is no extra differential term from $B[0]$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, dual terms in degree -n; section-hom-complexes, signed differential

proof.text: For each $n$, apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-finite-retract-dual-exact] to $T=E^{-n}$ with its specified splitting. Its dual splitting is precisely precomposition by $p_{-n}$ followed by precomposition by $i_{-n}$, and $i_{-n}^*p_{-n}^*=(p_{-n}i_{-n})^*=1$. Its coordinate-dual isomorphism identifies the intervening sheaf with $B^{\oplus N_{-n}}$. Under step 4 this gives the claimed finite-free retract structure on $D^n$. Apply the tensor argument of step 2 to that retract: $D^n\otimes_B-$ is exact, so each $D^n$ is flat as asserted.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, dual of a finite-free direct summand

proof.text: Both complexes now have flat terms and are bounded above: $E^r=0$ for $r>b$ and $D^n=0$ for $n>-a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] separately to $E^\bullet$ and $D^\bullet$, on the original small ringed site. They are K-flat for the sheaf tensor used here. For any module sheaf $M$, [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] therefore identifies their derived tensors with $M[0]$ with the ordinary complexes having terms $E^q\otimes_B M$ and $D^q\otimes_B M$, and differentials $d_E^q\otimes1$ and $d_D^q\otimes1$. In the second case use step 3 to identify the first derived factor with $E^\vee$. There is no flatness assumption on $M$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding K-flat construction

proof.text: The two ordinary tensor complexes from step 6 vanish termwise outside $[a,b]$ and $[-b,-a]$, respectively, since the tensor product of the zero sheaf with $M$ is zero by its defining universal property. For a degree $q$ outside the appropriate interval their degree-$q$ term is zero, so both its kernel of the outgoing differential and the image of the incoming differential are zero. The quotient $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$ is therefore zero. The definition of cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and the representing isomorphisms in step 6 yield both displayed Tor-window vanishings. This works for every $M$ on the site itself.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-6df92a1c5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item's 7 steps and every cited statement; no new nodes. The statement is unchanged (sha a5cbcc0e matches the unsplit version). It is a first split, not a re-split; the item came from Q95 2c51add3. Source checks in sites-cohomology.tex: 08JH l.11912, 08JJ l.13048, 06YQ l.3120, 08G1 l.12432 (2)=>(1). Step 1 uses finite-retract-dual-exact (finite r, pi=1); its last clause gives exactness of Hom(T,-). Step 2, accepted as elementary: tensor with a finite free module is a finite power, and a retract of an exact functor is exact. Step 3 uses bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso, which allows arbitrary complexes and so covers any K-injective resolution; D represents E^vee through the fixed resolution of def-pur-derived-internal-hom. Step 4 uses bounded-dual-components; I re-derived its sign (-1)^{n+1} from def-pur-hom-complex with target B[0]. Step 5 takes the dual splitting p*,i* and coordinate dual from finite-retract-dual-exact, and step 2 then gives flatness. Step 6: E and D are bounded above with flat terms, so bounded-flat-kflat makes them K-flat; kflat-single-tensor-comparison then allows any M. Step 7 is termwise vanishing. Edge cases tested: E=0, N=0, a single degree, two-term sign checks in degrees [-1,0] and [0,1], B=0. Advisory: partial overlap with lem-sfb-ringed-site-strict-perfect-hom. Tool_uses accepted: three generic tools from other units (exact-term Hom quasi-iso, 06YQ K-flatness on a site, K-flat tensor with a single sheaf). Batch-5 flag: lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison reaches only lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution (functorial flat resolutions on a site) and lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective (localizations are essentially surjective, 04VH/04VK). Both are generic homological/categorical facts, not steps of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so the citation is accepted. No SGA. Cosmetic: the report mentions citations.json and searches.jsonl, which are not in the commit.
